The gate hasn't judged the rule or its witnesses yet. Both runs returned `SCOPE_VIOLATION`, and the cause is in the harness, not in the two files.

**Why the gate fails:** its "changed outside the node's files" list held only the agent runtime's own temporary files under `.runtime/tmp/claude-154266/` (`tasks/*.output` and `cache-break-state-*.json`). They come from this session and the other coding sessions running at the same time. One of them is the output file of the gate command itself, and the second run created a new one. So every gate run inside a session will fail this check, whatever the files contain. I stopped after two runs and kept the other 4 in the budget. The harness's own run after the session ends should judge the files. To fix it for good, the scope check needs to ignore `.runtime/tmp/`.

**The rule** (`LVMC_11_30_070_B.lean`):
- **Who it covers:** a road user in the pedestrian aggregate `DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian`.
- **When it applies:** the place is declared a business district (`asm.business_district`) and the pedestrian occupies a roadway.
- **The duty:** if the pedestrian is moving across a lane or roadway it occupies, it must be in some crosswalk. "Moving across" uses `drv_motion_moving_across_carrier` with `p.halt_speed_tolerance` and `p.crossing_motion_cos`. The rule doesn't check whether the crosswalk is marked, so marked and unmarked crosswalks both count.
- I added no narrowing of my own; the reading of "cross" is the one the node already records.
- One choice the node left open: I didn't repeat "occupies a roadway" in the duty, because the applicability already requires it.

**The witnesses:** a pedestrian walks north at 1.4 m/s across a two-lane, two-way road. That is at right angles to the lanes, against a cosine limit of 0.94 and a minimum speed of 0.1 m/s.

| Scenario | Scene | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `forbid` | crosses with the only crosswalk 30 m away | violated |
| `permit` | crosses inside a marked crosswalk | compliant |
| `idle` | walks along the sidewalk, never on the roadway | not applicable |
| `blind` | same as `forbid`, with `kin.velocity` hidden | unknown |
| `branch_1` | crosses inside an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection | compliant |
| `branch_2` | same as `forbid`, but not a business district | not applicable |
| `branch_3` (added) | crosses a roadway with no lanes that carries its own direction | violated |

I added `branch_3` so the roadway part of "a lane or roadway" decides at least one scene. In the other scenes the roadway has no direction of its own, so only the lane part decides.

The full report is in `task_result.md` in the working directory.
